newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court upholds cable television law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court upholds cable television law.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday upheld a federal law that forces cable television firms to carry local broadcast stations.
The high court affirmed a ruling by three federal judges that the so-called must-carry cable television law does not violate constitutional free-speech protections.

The 1992 law required cable operators to devote as much as one third of their channels to local private and public broadcast stations. The law had been challenged in court by the cable industry as a form of illegal censorship.
The Supreme Court ruling was a victory for broadcasters and the U.S. Justice Department, which had defended the law.

Justice Anthony Kennedy said for the high court that the record supports the judgment by Congress that the must-carry provisions are consistent with the First Amendment and "further important government interests."

He added, "The must-carry provisions do not burden substantially more speech than is necessary to further the governmental interests they promote." Four of the court's nine members dissented from the ruling.
